source.title: Uncovering Cross-Linguistic Disparities in LLMs using Sparse Autoencoders
source.citation: Richmond Sin Jing Xuan et al., 2025
source.authors: Richmond Sin Jing Xuan; J. Huseynov; Yang Zhang

record.tranche_reason: The study uses Gemma Scope SAEs to analyze multilingual activations, but does not test superposition, feature competition for limited capacity, feature recovery, or feature geometry.
record.gate_note: The study reports SAE activation disparities and changes after activation-alignment fine-tuning. These results do not measure whether features overlap, are nearly orthogonal, or compete for dimensions, so they are recorded under fits_no_version rather than linked to a claim version. Benchmark results do not measure the claim's feature-representation mechanisms.
record.test_reason: The study uses off-the-shelf Gemma Scope SAEs as a tool to compare activation magnitudes across languages in Gemma-2-2B and to fine-tune for activation alignment. It never tests whether features are superposed, polysemantic, capacity-limited, recoverable by SAEs, canonical or one-dimensional. It only notes in related work that others have criticized SAEs, without testing that point.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that lower-resource languages receive systematically lower SAE activations despite similar embeddings, and that these gaps correlate with benchmark gaps (r about -0.95). Activation-alignment fine-tuning reduces the gaps, but task gains are limited and inconsistent: ARC-C rises while MMLU and HellaSwag fall for Malayalam. The abstract calls the improvements 'modest but consistent', which the appendix contradicts.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes SAE activations in a multilingual LLM and fine-tunes for activation alignment; it does not use the toy-network superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported activation disparity varies by layer, peaking at layer 6 and remaining at layer 25. Activation gains also vary by language and selected layer.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE feature activations are lower for medium-to-low resource languages than for high-resource ones in every layer: 26.27% lower at layer 6, 19.89% at layer 25 (Table 1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In Gemma-2-2B, SAE feature activations on translated text are lower for lower-resource languages, with the gap varying by layer.

fits_no_version.finding: LoRA fine-tuning with an activation-alignment loss raises non-English SAE activations: 43–94% at layer 20, and 68–89% across layers for Malayalam (Tables 5 and 7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-alignment fine-tuning raises SAE activations for non-English text.

fits_no_version.finding: Mean activation ratios relative to English range from 0.05 (Marathi) to 0.57 (Spanish) (Table 10).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE activation ratios relative to English vary by language in Gemma-2-2B.

record.problems: Evidence is limited to Gemma-2-2B. The paper notes that translation errors may misalign activations, and that activation alignment alone produces modest and inconsistent benchmark changes. It does not validate SAE features as complete or canonical units, nor measure superposition geometry.
record.rows_left_out: Benchmark scores and English activation-retention figures are not included because they do not measure the claim versions. The paper also reports some results only in figures; these are not needed to represent the tabulated SAE activation findings.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity transition or feature geometry.
No analysis of the causes of polysemanticity.
Uses pre-trained SAEs. Does not test feature recovery or the spread of features across neurons.
Cites SAE critiques (Till 2024; Anders et al. 2024) but does not test completeness, stability or canonicity.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T4 classification and its rows are correct. All rows measure activation magnitude on translated phrases and bear on no version. The paper's explicit reference to superposition and SAE validity is limited to related-work citations.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test sparse-feature superposition, overlap geometry, or sparsity-dependent transitions.
The study does not test capacity pressure, polysemanticity, or dedicated versus shared dimensions.
The study does not investigate alternative causes of polysemanticity.
It analyzes activations from existing Gemma Scope SAE features but does not test feature recovery or whether features are spread across neurons.
It does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
It does not measure whether features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: Treats SAE features as an analysis tool without evaluating feature recovery, superposition geometry, capacity pressure, canonicality or dimensionality.

tranche.reason: Uses Gemma Scope SAEs to measure cross-linguistic activation gaps and guide fine-tuning; does not test any superposition claim version.

source_check.notes: Activation gaps are group-mean differences divided by the high-resource group mean (Section 2.5), not measurements of superposition. Phrases were selected for high English SAE activation before translation; the authors acknowledge possible translation bias.
